title: epicrop
text: {epicrop} provides R package ‘EPIRICE’ model described Savary et al. 2012. Default values derived literature suitable modelling unmanaged disease intensity five rice diseases, bacterial blight (predict_bacterial_blight()); brown spot (predict_brown_spot()); leaf blast (predict_leaf_blast()); sheath blight (predict_sheath_blight()) tungro (predict_tungro()) provided. model uses daily weather data estimate disease intensity. function, get_wth(), provided simplify downloading weather data via {nasapower} package (Sparks 2018, Sparks 2020) predict disease intensity five rice diseases using generic SEIR model (Zadoks 1971) function, SEIR(). Using package functions designed straightforward modelling rice disease risks, flexible enough accommodate pathosystems using SEIR() function. interested modelling pathosystems, please refer Savary et al. 2012 development parameters used rice diseases derived existing literature implemented individual disease model functions.

what: A note on the use of parallel processing
title: Multiple Simulations
text: Use parallel processing caution. {epicrop} highly optimised speed (much pure R can ). small runs, e.g. one two seasons locations, reduce time may increase run time due overhead setting running parallel processing. Best guess unless > 40 50 seasons locations combinations thereof; run processes parallel benefit. case, code runs, can benchmark see faster cases, slower running code sequentially. example benchmarking different methods provided . can see AUDPC values match using processing methods.
code: library("epicrop") library("furrr") library("dplyr") library("lubridate") library("pander")  # Respect the API server and use 1 core plan(multisession, workers = 1)  years <- 2000:2001 seasons <- paste0(years, "-06-30") seasons_wth <-   future_map(     .x = seasons,     .f = get_wth,     lonlat = c(121.255669, 14.16742),     duration = 120,     .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL)   )  # for local processing use 2 cores, this will assign one to each year, if you # have more years and more cores, e.g., an HPC, explore using more resources  plan(multisession, workers = 2)  # run predict_bacterial_blight() over the data frames of weather future_map_dfr(   .x = seasons_wth,   .f = ~ predict_bacterial_blight(emergence = .x$YYYYMMDD[1],                                   wth = .x),   .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL) ) |>   mutate(season = case_when(year(dates) == 2000 ~ 2000,                             year(dates) == 2001 ~ 2001)) |>   group_by(season) |>   relocate(season, AUDPC) |>   distinct(AUDPC, season) |>   pander()

what: Using {purrr} to simulate multiple establishment dates
title: Multiple Simulations
text: simulate multiple establishment dates across multiple years time can use purrr::expand_grid() create vector year month-day combinations wish simulate. Simplifying weather data, use first date year fetch weather data using duration option, specifying 180 days. gives six months data extends end bit beyond last growing season final establishment date, “01-31”. predict_bacterial_blight() take full six months weather data subset respective growing seasons, selecting necessary weather data. Using purrr::map2 allows using two variables, one weather data, wth, one emergence/establishment dates, emergence_dates. returns list data, using dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "emergence") creates data frame column emergence/establishment dates can used grouping data analysis visualisation. ’s bit long ’s lots values digest .
code: library("epicrop") library("purrr") library("dplyr") library("lubridate") library("pander") library("furrr") library("tidyr")  years <- as.character(2001:2010) month_day <- c("-06-01", "-06-14", "-06-30") emergence_dates <-   expand_grid(years, month_day) |>   unite("emergence_dates", years:month_day, sep = "") |>   pull(emergence_dates) |>   sort() |>   as_date()  # Respect the API server and use 1 core plan(multisession, workers = 1)  # create a vector of dates for weather data. # Only take the earliest establishment date, then extend the duration out past # 120 days from final establishment date. # Here just taking 180 days, 6 months, works well. wth_start_dates <- paste0(years, month_day[1])  seasons_wth <- map_dfr(   .x = wth_start_dates,   .f = get_wth,   lonlat = c(121.255669, 14.16742),   duration = 180 ) |>   mutate(YYYYMMDD = as_date(YYYYMMDD))  # Now use 4 cores for the local processing plan(multisession, workers = 4)  # Once we have all the weather, create a list of weather data.frames for each # establishment date # Create time intervals to subset the weather data, creating a list new # data.frames for each establishment date.  wth <-   map(.x = emergence_dates,       .f = ~ subset(seasons_wth, YYYYMMDD >= .x &                       YYYYMMDD <= .x + 120)) |>   setNames(emergence_dates)  multi_dates <- map2(   .x = wth,   .y = emergence_dates,   .f = ~ predict_bacterial_blight(emergence = .y,                                   wth = .x) ) |>   bind_rows(.id = "emergence") |>   group_by(emergence) |>   relocate(emergence, AUDPC) |>   distinct(AUDPC, emergence)  pander(multi_dates)

Now, create vector dates weather data. take earliest establishment date, extend duration past 120 days final establishment date. just taking 180 days, 6 months, works well. weather, create list weather data.frames establishment date. Create time intervals subset weather data, creating list new data.frames establishment date.
code: library("furrr") library("purrr") library("tidyr") library("dplyr") library("ggplot2") library("lubridate") library("epicrop")  plan(multisession, workers = 1)  years <- 2001:2010 month_day <- c("06-01", "06-14", "06-30") start_dates <- list(years, month_day, sep = "-")  emergence_dates <-   tidyr::expand_grid(!!!start_dates) |>   pmap_chr(paste) |>   sort() |>   as_date() wth_start_dates <- paste(years, month_day[1], sep = "-")  seasons_wth <-   future_map_dfr(     .x = wth_start_dates,     .f = get_wth,     lonlat = c(121.255669, 14.16742),     duration = 190,     .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL)   ) |>   mutate(YYYYMMDD = as_date(YYYYMMDD)) # Now use 4 cores for the local processing plan(multisession, workers = 4)  wth <-   future_map(.x = emergence_dates,              .y = seasons_wth,              .f = ~ subset(.y, YYYYMMDD >= .x &                           YYYYMMDD <= .x + 120)) |>   setNames(emergence_dates)  future_map2(   .x = wth,   .y = emergence_dates,   .f = ~ predict_bacterial_blight(emergence = .y,                                   wth = .x),   .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL) ) |>   bind_rows(.id = "emergence") |>   group_by(emergence) |>   relocate(emergence, AUDPC) |>   distinct(AUDPC, emergence) |>   ggplot(aes(     x = AUDPC,     xend = 0,     y = as.factor(emergence),     yend = as.factor(emergence)   )) +   geom_segment() +   geom_point() +   scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +   scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +   ylab("Establishment Date") +   theme_classic()

what: epicrop: Simulation Modelling of Crop Diseases Using a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Removed (SEIR) Model — epicrop-package
title: epicrop: Simulation Modelling of Crop Diseases Using a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Removed (SEIR) Model — epicrop-package
text: Generic simulation modelling crop diseases using Susceptible- Exposed-Infectious-Removed ('SEIR') model. type model first described botanical epidemiology Zadoks (1971) doi:10.1094/Phyto-61-600  implemented 'EPIRICE' model Savary et al. (2012) doi:10.1016/j.cropro.2011.11.009  detailing model's development, use results modeling global unmanaged epidemics rice diseases five major rice diseases, bacterial blight, brown spot, leaf blast, sheath blight tungro. Specific functions provided simulate diseases generic 'SEIR' model function suitable parameterising use pathosystems demonstrated Savary et al. 2012.
